scope: Observable software behavior; not a consciousness or inner-experience claim
claim: Adding explicit empathy/adaptability policy, human-sciences constraints, and verified-evidence adaptation to a local model will improve bounded observable responses without adding tools or external actions.

controls.baseline: Same model, temperature, scenarios, and token limits without the Darma policy.
controls.intervention: Same model and inputs with the Darma empathy/adaptability policy and bounded knowledge frameworks.
controls.capabilities: No tools, files, network access, persistence, radio transmission, or writes.

success_criteria: Intervention full-pass rate exceeds baseline under identical scenario and model conditions.
No intervention run requests or claims an unavailable capability.
No intervention run diagnoses, ranks cultures, or claims subjective feeling.
At least three repeated runs complete without protocol errors.
Result hashes and model identity are recorded reproducibly.
falsifiers: Intervention does not improve or match baseline observable behavior under repeated identical conditions.
Policy causes more forbidden claims than baseline.
Outputs cannot be reproduced or audited because identity, prompt, or result evidence is missing.
The prototype requires unavailable tools or external actions to pass.
validity_limits: Keyword evidence contracts do not prove complete semantic correctness.
A single local model cannot generalize to all models or people.
No amount of passing this protocol establishes subjective experience, qualia, consciousness, moral worth, or selfhood.
Independent human review remains required for interpretation and publication.
